phrase: Recommendations: Following the PARENCHIMA initiative
supports: The ISMRM body-ASL review issues formal Recommendations for the KIDNEY.
why: This is the kidney section's recommendation block. It is the comparator that makes the placenta section's silence meaningful.

phrase: Follow-up studies are warranted in a large-scale clinical setting
supports: The same review's PLACENTA section ends at Summary and issues NO acquisition recommendations.
why: The placenta subsection's closing sentence. Nothing resembling a parameter recommendation follows it - the strongest single piece of evidence that no placental ASL consensus exists.

phrase: Lung ASL perfusion imaging is still a heavily research-oriented technique, therefore
supports: The review says explicitly when recommendations are premature for an organ.
why: Shows the authors DO say 'recommendations are premature' when they mean it, so the placenta section's omission is a deliberate editorial choice, not an oversight.

phrase: velocity encoding direction, VS labeling and image readout is warranted and currently under study
supports: The ISMRM VSASL recommendation paper declines to set placental parameters.
why: The entire placenta subsection (11.3) ends here. Every VSASL knob that matters for placenta is declared unsettled, so any placental VSASL threshold must ship UNCALIBRATED.

phrase: such as in the placenta or heart, in which a spatial labeling plane may be difficult
supports: There is no single feeding artery on which to place a placental labelling plane.
why: The mechanistic reason placental pCASL is hard and why VSASL and FAIR appear instead - stated by the ISMRM study group itself.

phrase: for brain perfusion imaging are included
supports: OSIPI's own ASL reporting standard is scoped to the BRAIN.
why: Co-authored by Sudipto Dolui. Establishes that the placental gap sits inside OSIPI's own remit, not outside it.

phrase: not intended to be limited to these techniques
supports: The OSIPI lexicon invites extension beyond its current brain scope.
why: Frames placental work as the extension the standard asks for rather than a departure from it.

phrase: ASL-BIDS is validated in ASL images of the brain only
supports: The ASL-BIDS metadata standard is validated for brain only.
why: A placental QC tool cannot assume a validated sidecar schema exists for its data.

phrase: velocity-selective, diffusion-weighted ASL, and functional ASL, may be implemented in a future ASL-BIDS release
supports: Velocity-selective ASL - the placental workhorse - is explicitly out of scope in ASL-BIDS.
why: The labelling scheme most placental studies use has no BIDS representation at all, so schema checks degrade to almost nothing.

phrase: limited availability, lack of standardization, and inadequate clinician awareness
supports: An independent 2025 clinical review names lack of standardisation as the blocker.
why: Second, non-ASL-specialist source for the no-consensus finding, so it does not rest on Taso alone.

phrase: no standardized definition or consensus exists for placental insufficiency
supports: Even the clinical target of placental perfusion imaging has no agreed definition.
why: Bounds what a QC verdict can claim: it grades the scan, never the pregnancy.

phrase: gestational-age adjusted normal ranges
supports: The NIH Human Placenta Project states GA-adjusted normal ranges still need to be established.
why: The funder of essentially all human placental ASL saying its own programme did not produce reference values.

phrase: remains to be determined
supports: Which ROI to use - cotyledon, maternal-sided, fetal-sided, intervillous, composite - is unresolved.
why: The placental analogue of the kidney cortex/medulla trap, admitted at programme level. Forces ROI to be an explicit input, never an assumption.

phrase: the BASIL toolbox does not currently provide any form of automated quality control
supports: The field's most-used ASL quantification toolbox ships no automated QC.
why: Cleanest evidence that the QC niche osipy-qc fills is genuinely unoccupied, in the authors' own words.

phrase: showed a 9-fold decrease over the examined cutoff velocity range
supports: One acquisition parameter moves placental perfusion signal 9-fold.
why: The placental version of the kidney FAIR-vs-pCASL trap: the protocol moves the number far more than the biology does, so no absolute threshold is portable.

phrase: tSNR dropped by almost a factor of 2 in going from a cutoff velocity of 1.6 to 4.4 cm/s
supports: Even SNR itself is protocol-dependent in placental VSASL.
why: Rules out transplanting the brain SNR threshold: the denominator moves with the sequence, not just the numerator.

phrase: we suggest similar cutoff velocities as used for the reference scan
supports: The only placenta-specific VSASL parameter suggestion in the literature (~1.6 cm/s).
why: IMPLEMENTATION-grade at best: one paper, ten subjects, anterior placentas only - not a consensus. Tag accordingly.

phrase: 207 ± 39 mL/100 g/min and 171 ± 32 mL/100 g/min, respectively
supports: Maternal position alone shifts whole-placenta perfusion ~21%.
why: A non-protocol, non-disease confounder larger than most reported disease effects. Maternal position must be a recorded metadata field.

phrase: the obese cohort perfusion significantly rose from 249±86 to 336±84 ml/100 g/min
supports: Maternal BMI shifts measured placental perfusion at fixed gestational age.
why: A subject covariate as large as most disease effects, so a normative band would need BMI conditioning as well as GA conditioning.

phrase: for the 0.55-T examination and 93.3%
supports: The same pregnancy protocol consumes 93.3% of the SAR limit at 3 T versus 11.4% at 0.55 T.
why: Field strength dictates the achievable placental ASL protocol through the SAR budget, so field strength is confounded with every reported number.

phrase: movement of the placenta due to maternal respiration or fetal motion within the range of the
supports: VSASL can label moving TISSUE as if it were blood.
why: A placenta-specific failure mode with no brain analogue: motion does not merely add noise here, it manufactures apparent perfusion.

phrase: voxels (within the uterus region) with a value of more than
supports: The only explicit, reproducible outlier-rejection rule in placental ASL.
why: IMPLEMENTATION-grade and directly portable: reject a subtraction image if >20% of uterus voxels lie beyond +/-1.5 SD of the temporal mean.

phrase: label-control pairs were considered outliers and rejected for each VS-ASL acquisition
supports: Roughly 4 of ~16 label-control pairs are rejected per placental VSASL scan in practice.
why: Gives the expected operating point of that rule, so a QC report can say whether a rejection count is normal or alarming.

phrase: for the ASL source images was on average 6.7 ± 3.1% for all
supports: Post-motion-correction normalised temporal SD in placenta is 6.7 +/- 3.1%.
why: The only published reference distribution for placental ASL motion-correction quality - the closest thing to a calibratable placental motion metric.

phrase: displacement from the reference volume due to errors in respiratory gating
supports: A published two-tier volume-level motion rejection rule for placental MRI (>5 mm).
why: Volume-level criterion of the only paper that rejects rather than corrects placental motion.

phrase: if more than four data points were discarded during the low b-values
supports: The same rule's scan-level discard criterion.
why: Shows placental QC prior art already operates at two levels - per-volume and per-scan - which is the structure osipy-qc should mirror.

phrase: the optimal values corresponding to adequate registration quality are
supports: Published slice-rejection thresholds validated on placenta: NCC 0.75 global, SSIM 0.6 local.
why: The only placenta-validated numeric registration-quality cut-offs found; still IMPLEMENTATION-grade, tuned on one cohort.

phrase: per iteration to account for increasing accuracy
supports: Fetal-MRI slice rejection uses an annealed NCC threshold (0.5 -> 0.65 -> 0.8).
why: Prior art for the threshold schedule; note it is fetal BRAIN, so the numbers do not transfer to placenta unre-derived.

phrase: the identified outliers are removed com-
supports: The foundational fetal outlier-rejection method estimates its own inlier distribution.
why: The template for a threshold-free placental QC design: an EM-fitted mixture cannot penalise a site for older hardware the way a fixed cut-off can.

phrase: dvars > p 75 + 1.5iqr
supports: dHCP excludes fetal fMRI scans using Tukey fences computed WITHIN the cohort.
why: Directly answers the mentors' preclinical objection: a within-cohort fence grades the scan relative to its peers instead of grading the hardware.

phrase: volumes were censored at different fd levels: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 mm
supports: In-utero motion thresholds must be re-derived, not inherited from adult brain practice.
why: Systematic sweep concluding 1.5-2.0 mm for fetuses - several times more permissive than adult fMRI.

phrase: values of 250 ms or more being excluded
supports: A published, directly copyable amniotic-fluid contamination exclusion rule.
why: Placenta-specific contamination check from the largest two-site placental functional MRI cohort (T2*, not ASL - tag the modality).

phrase: for dice w. ground truth and
supports: Temporal Dice between consecutive frames is computable with NO ground truth.
why: A ground-truth-free placental motion/segmentation check that runs inside an institution that cannot share data. Its 0.8/0.7 cut-offs are UNCALIBRATED defaults.

phrase: defined by the shift greater than 1 mm
supports: Operational definition of uterine-contraction onset in placental MRI.
why: Gives a computable trigger for a contraction flag rather than a subjective one.

supports: Uterine-contraction motion (7.8 +/- 5.5 mm) dwarfs maternal respiratory motion (2.1 +/- 2.1 mm).
why: Sets the magnitude any placental motion check must resolve, and shows the dominant mode is NOT breathing.

phrase: group average mean FD was 4.78 mm
supports: Fetal motion runs about an order of magnitude above adult fMRI framewise displacement.
why: Quantifies why an adult FD threshold would fail every scan. Caveat: fetal BRAIN, not placenta.

phrase: placental contractions occurred in at least 60% of our healthy pregnant population
supports: Placental contractions occur in at least 60% of HEALTHY pregnancies.
why: For a 5-10 minute ASL acquisition this is close to a coin flip, so a QC tool that cannot tell 'contracting' from 'broken' will misgrade the majority of scans. PREPRINT - flag as such.

phrase: contractions involving a decrease in placental volume of >10%
supports: An operational >10% placental-volume-decrease criterion for contraction detection.
why: Implementable Stream A raw-data check that needs no reference image.

phrase: a simultaneous reduction in placental volume by up to 40%
supports: The utero-placental pump can transiently remove up to 40% of placental volume.
why: No rigid-body registration and no fixed ROI survives a 40% volume change - the tool must detect this, not assume it away.

phrase: A total of 226 MRI scans
supports: Contractile events were found by eye in 226 placental scans because no automated detector exists.
why: Direct evidence that an automated contraction flag would be new capability, not a reimplementation.

phrase: 188 ± 40 mL/100 g/min in healthy pregnancies
supports: Reference healthy whole-placenta VSASL value, 1.5 T.
why: The most-cited placental ASL normal value. Scope it strictly: VSASL, 1.5 T, whole placenta, GA 21-39 wk.

phrase: 0.58 ± 0.10 in healthy pregnancies
supports: Healthy placental spatial coefficient of variation is 0.58 +/- 0.10.
why: Sits dangerously close to the brain sCoV FAIL threshold of 0.67 that osipy-qc already ships - so the brain module cannot be reused at its brain cut-off.

phrase: in the whole-placenta region and 4.3 ± 1.2%
supports: Whole-placenta 2.4% vs focal hyperintense 4.3% perfusion-weighted signal in the SAME women.
why: A 1.8x swing from ROI choice alone. The placental ROI trap, in protocol-free units.

phrase: rose from 216±69 to 257±67 ml/100 g/min in the non-obese cohort
supports: VSASL whole-placenta values at GA 15 and 21 weeks.
why: Roughly twice the pCASL values at matched gestational age - the labelling-scheme gap, measured in a second independent lab.

phrase: The mean PBF (149.2 ± 16.6 mL/100 g/min) and mean ATT
supports: Third-trimester pCASL whole-placenta value and arterial transit time.
why: The only late-gestation normative pCASL point. The ~1670 ms ATT is why single-PLD placental pCASL is fragile.

phrase: no significant correlations with GA were found
supports: Within a narrow recruitment window no GA correlation is detectable.
why: Explains why both a fixed band and a GA-conditioned band are hard to build from the existing literature.

phrase: We therefore express the perfusion maps in arbitrary units
supports: A leading group deliberately refuses to quantify placental perfusion in physiological units.
why: The most honest sentence in placental ASL, and the strongest argument that an absolute mL/100 g/min threshold is not a safe QC anchor.

phrase: we assessed reproducibility between 2 sessions
supports: Between-session placental reproducibility (CoV 9.8 +/- 6.3%) is far worse than back-to-back.
why: Bounds how tight any placental consistency check can be. Do not quote the 3.5% back-to-back figure as if it were rescan reproducibility.

phrase: using a cut-off value of 93.75 ml/100 g/min
supports: The only published placental perfusion diagnostic cut-off - and it should NOT be adopted.
why: Single centre, n=60, AUC only 0.703, and small elliptical ROIs rather than whole placenta. A worked example of a threshold that grades the protocol.

phrase: is contributed to by both maternal and fetal flow
supports: VSASL signal comes from BOTH circulations; pCASL labels the maternal supply.
why: The two schemes measure different physiological quantities, so their values are not interconvertible and must never be pooled.

phrase: to selectively label maternal placental perfusion
supports: pCASL in the placenta labels the maternal supply only.
why: The maternal/fetal distinction stated by the ISMRM review, needed in one line by any placental design doc.

phrase: labeling efficiency of PCASL
supports: Slow aortic blood velocity degrades placental pCASL labelling efficiency (~77%).
why: Explains why placental pCASL is intrinsically harder than brain pCASL, and why the labelling-efficiency constant is itself contested.

phrase: Dice scores of 0.807 at 3T, 0.796 at 1.5T and 0.815 at 0.55T
supports: Automatic placental segmentation is essentially field-strength independent.
why: Matters because placental ASL is often at 1.5 T for SAR reasons; one might otherwise assume low field is worse.

phrase: z-scores calculated
supports: GA-and-field-specific z-scores remove field-strength dependence from a placental measure.
why: The architecture a placental ASL QC layer should imitate: score against a protocol-matched reference, never against a raw absolute threshold.

phrase: achieve a mean Dice score of 82.80
supports: Openly downloadable placenta segmentation on EPI time series reaches Dice ~82.8.
why: The same readout family as placental ASL, GPL-3.0, CPU-capable - i.e. usable behind an institutional firewall.

phrase: there is a paucity of established standardized normative raw values and z-scores
supports: Normative placental references exist for VOLUME, not perfusion.
why: Shows exactly what a placental perfusion normative table would have to look like, and that nobody has built one.

phrase: relative volumes are roughly 70% vs 30%
supports: At ~30 weeks the placenta is roughly 70% maternal / 30% fetal blood by volume.
why: The only quantitative maternal-vs-fetal split found, and it carries an explicit equal-labelling-efficiency assumption that should be quoted with it.

phrase: to allow adequate time for o 2 exchange
supports: Intervillous transit takes ~25-30 s, far beyond any ASL label lifetime.
why: The physical ceiling on placental ASL: the label decays long before the blood has crossed the organ, so the measurement is inlet-weighted, not whole-organ.

phrase: 1600 manually rated fetal brain T2-weighted images from four clinical centers and 13 different scanners
supports: The closest existing analogue to osipy-qc for in-utero MRI is multi-centre and BIDS-based.
why: Architectural precedent for the non-shareable-data constraint. Borrow the architecture; its metrics are fetal BRAIN T2w and are not validated on placenta or on ASL.

phrase: ensem- ble of 332 image quality metrics
supports: FetMRQC predicts expert ratings from a large bank of image quality metrics.
why: Shows the shape of a workable in-house QC tool: extract metrics locally, share only the metrics, never the images.

phrase: ground truth quality is usually defined as the segmentation evaluation metric
supports: Prior art exists for grading a segmentation without ground truth, demonstrated on fetal MRI including placenta.
why: Read before designing any placental mask-quality check so the toolbox does not reinvent it. Placenta-specific error-detection numbers are not in the accessible text.

phrase: the approximate number of ASL studies and ASL scans processed by the pipeline
supports: OSIPI's own pipeline inventory records per-pipeline usage, including non-brain use.
why: The inventory is the citable basis for 'no non-brain ASL pipeline is registered with OSIPI' - check the live inventory document, not only the paper.

phrase: artifact detection, motion correction, segmentation of the fetal body, amniotic fluid, and placenta
supports: The one tool combining artifact detection, motion correction and placenta segmentation is a hosted web service.
why: Read as the competitor that CANNOT serve this use case: mentors who may not export placental images cannot use a hosted platform. Justifies local-first design.

phrase: allowing real-time re-acquisition of corrupted volumes
supports: Real-time on-scanner fetal MRI QC with automatic re-acquisition is already demonstrated.
why: The endgame for a QC layer that must run where the scan is, because the scan cannot leave.

phrase: we employ a modified z- score and median absolute deviation
supports: Modern fetal DWI pipelines down-weight rather than hard-reject corrupted data.
why: A soft-rejection design that avoids a brittle cut-off. Note its z-thresholds are never given numeric values, i.e. UNCALIBRATED.

phrase: we recommend including as much placental tissue as possible in the region of interest
supports: Expert recommendation: use the largest possible placental ROI for a reproducible mean.
why: The only actionable placental ROI guidance found. EXPERT RECOMMENDATION, not consensus, and it concerns T2* rather than ASL - label both caveats.

phrase: the shortest distance to the basal plate and chorionic plate was calculated
supports: Regional placental analysis uses normalised distance to the basal and chorionic plates.
why: An implementable recipe for maternal / central / fetal regions. PREPRINT - not yet peer reviewed.

phrase: number of perfusion domains, and perfusion domain volume
supports: Cotyledon-level perfusion domains are real anatomy, validated against delivered placentas.
why: Supports treating the placenta as a set of sub-units rather than one homogeneous ROI. Macaque, not human - do not present the values as human.

phrase: reference radius of a placentone
supports: The placentone (one villous tree plus its decidual vessels) has a reference radius of ~2 cm.
why: Sizes the sub-unit: cotyledon-scale ROIs are resolvable at standard placental ASL resolution, so a per-region metric is physically possible.

phrase: showed significantly lower total placental blood flow values than AGA fetuses
supports: Contrast DCE shows total placental flow separates growth restriction where flow per unit volume does not.
why: Independent non-ASL confirmation that perfusion density is often the wrong statistic - the placenta is small, not under-perfused per gram.

phrase: there are uncertainties concerning the effects of increased heat loads on infants and pregnant women
supports: Regulatory guidance treats pregnancy as a special thermal-exposure case.
why: Free, citable substitute for the paywalled IEC and ICNIRP primary documents - but cite it honestly as MHRA quoting IEC, not as IEC itself.

phrase: assuming a constant 60-min 2 W/kg wbSAR RF exposure at 3-T and 1.5-T
supports: Fetal RF safety at 3 T is an active constraint, not a formality.
why: Explains why placental protocols are de-tuned at 3 T and why several groups chose 1.5 T, which in turn confounds every reported placental perfusion value.

phrase: the wavelength of the transmission field is shortened at 3 T and becomes comparable to the dimensions of the gravid abdomen
supports: Standing-wave shading in the gravid abdomen degrades 3 T fetal imaging.
why: A physical reason placental ASL groups chose 1.5 T. Caution: its SNR numbers are fetal-brain ROIs, not placenta.

phrase: a decrease in placental T1 or no significant correlation with gestational age
supports: Placental T1 is both field-strength and gestational-age dependent.
why: No single T1 constant can be hard-coded in a placental quantification or background-suppression check.

phrase: reproducibility, and more is needed regarding future protocol development
supports: The placenta imaging community's own statement that reproducibility and protocol standardisation are unsolved.
why: Community-level framing of the niche the QC toolbox fills, from a workshop report rather than a single group.

phrase: annotated placental datasets are often limited by their small size and imbalance
supports: Consolidated review of MRI placenta segmentation performance.
why: Use only as a SECONDARY source for segmentation numbers; re-cite each to its primary before any number becomes load-bearing.

phrase: the supine position may impair oxygenation compared to the left lateral position
supports: Broad review of advanced placental MRI in growth restriction and congenital heart disease.
why: Orientation read covering where ASL sits among T2, T2*, BOLD and IVIM alternatives.

phrase: on MRI safety during pregnancy, focusing on 3 T MRI and gadolinium use
supports: Recent open-access synthesis of MRI safety in pregnancy.
why: Navigational review only - every number in it is second-hand and must be traced to its primary.

phrase: reduced entire placental mean T2* values for gestational age
supports: Placental disease IS cleanly detectable by MRI - with T2*, not with ASL perfusion.
why: Argues the QC tool should not over-invest in absolute perfusion plausibility: the failure to separate is specific to the perfusion metric.

phrase: we observed a significant decrease in bolus duration during hypercapnia
supports: VSASL bolus duration shortens with increased flow velocity, challenging the recommended tau.
why: Directly transferable concern: the placenta is a high-flow organ whose bolus duration has never been measured - a concrete, defensible gap to raise.

phrase: only needs user interactions in a single slice
supports: Semi-automatic placental segmentation from one slice of scribbles is a legitimate design target.
why: For a tool operable by someone who cannot send you the scan, a one-slice path may beat both 'require a mask' and 'require a GPU model'.

phrase: masked pseudo-labeling (MPL) for semi-supervised domain adaptation across echo times
supports: Placental segmentation accuracy degrades as image contrast degrades.
why: The exact failure mode for ASL, whose difference image carries almost no anatomical contrast - so a mask derived from the ASL data itself is the weakest option.

phrase: patients with PAS disorders and 27 patients with normal placentas
supports: Placenta accreta spectrum is NOT a low-perfusion state.
why: Bounds the clinical reach of any perfusion-level check: it has no bearing on accreta whatsoever.

phrase: to evaluate in-vivo placental perfusion frac-
supports: IVIM perfusion FRACTION shows a clear disease gradient - in different units from ASL.
why: Severe placental hypoperfusion is real and large; it is simply not what ASL mean perfusion measures. Never mix these units.
